summary: Bridget Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Cape Town and earned a PhD from University College London under Frederick Zeuner. She was a fellow at Wolfson College, Cambridge, and served as secretary and chairman of the Ancient India & Iran Trust.
Brigitte Marschall earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she later held a post as professor (attested 2010).

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Bronwyn Finnigan studied at Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland, completing doctoral research under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop. She held posts at Auckland (~2008–2014), Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn, a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religion, studied at the University of Chicago and earned his PhD from the University of Michigan. He taught at Northwestern University (~2003–2012), the National University of Singapore (~2012–2013), and the University of Chicago (~2013).
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bruce B. Lawrence, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at Princeton University, the Fay School, and the Episcopal Divinity School. He served as a professor at Duke University from approximately 1971 to 2014.

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.
Bruce John Stewart studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Sakya College in 1978 and earned a PhD from Columbia University under Alex Wayman, Joel Peter Brereton, and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln is a scholar of religion, history, and archaeology who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held faculty posts at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and the University of Chicago (~1993).
Bruce M. Knauft studied at the University of Michigan (~1976–1983). He has served as Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology at Emory University (~1985).
Bruce M. Sullivan, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen from ~1975 to 1979. He held a faculty post at Northern Arizona University from ~1986 to 2020.

Bruce Matthews, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, completed graduate studies at McMaster University. He was a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Peradeniya and served as professor of comparative religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).

Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 1988) and Wheaton College, where he is attested in 2019 as associate professor of anthropology.

Bruno Dagens, a scholar of archaeology and Indology, studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, UCLouvain, the French Institute of Pondicherry, KU Leuven (~1977–1986), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Munich, Breslau, and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He taught as professor at the University of Breslau (attested 1902; 1921–1928) and later held a post at Heidelberg University (~1928–1939).
Bruno Lindner was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig University and under Rudolf von Roth. From 1878 to 1919, he served as a Privatdozent at Leipzig University.

Bruno Petzold, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, studied at Leipzig University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Daito Shimaji and Hikoshiro Hoshino. In Japan, he taught at First Higher School, Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.
Bryan D. Lowe, a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religion, studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone. He held an academic post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

Bryan J. Cuevas studied at Emory University and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Princeton and became John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University (attested 2008–2021).
